results.message:
fix(docs): render the README example the way a real terminal shows it

The tables in the `audit` example came out with square corners because the block
was generated on a console where rich reports legacy_windows=True: it substitutes
box characters it decides the terminal cannot draw, so box.ROUNDED — which is what
the code asks for — renders square there and rounded everywhere else. The rounded
corners the README already had were correct, and regenerating the block replaced
them with the wrong glyphs.

The CI caught it, which is what the test was added for, and then the test itself
was the thing that failed: it compared the document against whatever console the
machine happened to provide. It now renders through a console it declares — 80
columns, no colour, legacy_windows=False — so the same bytes come out on any
machine, and a new assertion fails if that rendering is ever substituted again.
The same run of the suite is what SonarCloud reports on, so both workflows were
red for this one reason.

ci: install the declared extra, instead of a list written by hand

sonarcloud.yml ran `pip install -e .` and then named its pytest plugins one by
one, rather than installing the extra this project declares. That gave it a
different set of packages from tests.yml, and a set nothing keeps in step with
pyproject.toml — so adding hypothesis broke the SonarCloud run with
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hypothesis'` while the test workflow, which
does install the extra, stayed green. codspeed.yml had the same shape and passes
today only because it collects tests/benchmarks alone; it is corrected too,
rather than left as the next one to break.

pytest-codspeed keeps its own line: it is a plugin for that one workflow and is
not a dependency of the project.

tests/test_ci_dependencies.py is the guard. Every workflow that invokes pytest
must install the declared extra, and must not name a package pyproject.toml does
not control. Its detector has to tell a distribution from a flag and from the
editable target, so it carries the cases that prove it does — `-e ".[dev]"`,
`--only-binary :all:` and a quoted version specifier all had to stop being read
as package names before the rule said anything true.

The rule also found a redundancy it was not looking for: tests.yml installed
pytest, pytest-cov, pytest-asyncio and pytest-timeout on top of the extra that
already declares all four.
